articles.title: Rep. Jim Clyburn says impeaching Trump shouldn’t be Democrats’ priority if win back the House
articles.summary: Rep. Jim Clyburn, D-S.C., said that Democrats should not prioritize impeaching President Donald Trump if they win control of the House in the upcoming midterm elections, but instead should focus on making life more affordable
articles.body: Rep. Jim Clyburn, D-S.C., on Sunday said that Democrats should not prioritize impeaching President Donald Trump if they win control of the House in the upcoming midterm elections, but instead should focus on making life more affordable for Americans. Clyburn told NBC News’ “Meet the Press” that if Democrats take back the House he feels confident that their first order of business would be making the country accessible and affordable for all citizens. Pressed on whether he believes Democrats should rule out the prospect of impeaching Trump if they regain control of the House, the South Carolina lawmaker said, “I don’t rule it out, but I don’t rule it in.” He added, “I don’t think that should be our priority if we get into office. Our priority ought to be making housing, education, energy, healthcare affordable and accessible for all of our citizens. Impeaching the president will not do that.” His remarks come days after House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., was asked a similar question by CNN and said that he wasn’t ruling out impeaching Trump. “We haven’t ruled anything in and we haven’t ruled anything out,” Jeffries told CNN, adding that he’s leaving those decisions up to the Democrats that would be in charge of the House Oversight and Judiciary committees if Democrats take back the House. “As we’ve done in the past, whenever there have been moments of accountability that we’ve had to lead on, we are guided by three principles: follow the facts, apply the law and be guided by the United States Constitution,” the minority leader added. House Democrats impeached Trump twice during his first term, but the Senate did not vote to convict him either time. Clyburn on Sunday also spoke about Justice Clarence Thomas, who has been a crucial part of the Supreme Court’s conservative wing since he was first nominated by former President George H.W. Bush in 1991. During the confirmation process in 1991, Clyburn advocated for Thomas to be confirmed, telling a panel of senators at the time, “It’s a pleasure for me to be here today to present testimony in favor of my good friend Clarence Thomas. I have known Clarence for 10 years, and I consider him to be a personal and professional friend, in spite of the fact that he shares a conservative Republican philosophy.” On Sunday, Clyburn denounced his support of Thomas three decades ago, telling “Meet the Press,” “I have made mistakes in my life, and that’s one that I made, and I will own up to that mistake.” “I had no idea that Clarence Thomas would rebel the way he has against his own background and experiences,” the South Carolina congressman added. Asked whether he supported a proposal from former Vice President Kamala Harris to expand the Supreme Court from nine justices to 13, Clyburn said, “I do.” He added, “I think that we are in a position now that calls for some significant actions taken by the Congress, and we ought to expand it. Thirteen is a pretty good number; a baker’s dozen will be a good number to have on the court.”

articles.title: Trump just brokered a deal with the country sitting atop the world’s largest oil reserves
articles.summary: President Donald Trump's Venezuela oil deal targets 65 billion barrels across 17 fields, but major infrastructure hurdles stand before pump relief.
articles.body: President Donald Trump’s new oil agreement with Venezuela could give the United States access to a 65 billion-barrel crude-oil prize — an energy-security win, even if drivers are unlikely to see benefits quickly. The deal announced Friday would give the U.S. a stake in 17 Venezuelan oil fields holding an estimated 65 billion barrels of crude, according to Venezuela’s government. Venezuela controls more than 300 billion barrels of crude reserves, roughly 20% of the world’s total. It is the largest oil stockpile on the planet, exceeding even Saudi Arabia’s. TRUMP'S AMBITIOUS ENERGY BET COULD BE A WINNING HAND AS THE WORLD BURNS MORE OIL, GAS THAN EVER Yet Venezuela has long struggled to turn that oil wealth into steady production. Political instability and deteriorating infrastructure have left the country producing only about 1% of the world’s oil despite holding an estimated 17% of global reserves. For Trump, the potential benefit goes beyond the deal’s headline number. Venezuela produces heavy crude, the type many Gulf Coast refineries were designed to process. Much U.S. production is lighter shale crude, while Gulf Coast refiners have historically relied on heavier imports from Canada, Mexico and Venezuela. TOP ENERGY TRADER HAILS TRUMP'S VENEZUELA OIL DEAL AS A 'GENERATIONAL WIN' FOR GAS PRICES A steadier Venezuelan supply could support Gulf Coast refineries, diversify U.S. oil imports and provide a buffer against future supply disruptions. It could also help replenish the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, which remains well below its 714 million-barrel authorized capacity. That prospect has taken on added importance as the war with Iran disrupts oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. The average U.S. price for regular gasoline stood at about $4.07 a gallon Sunday, according to AAA, compared with roughly $3.19 a year earlier. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP For Trump, the deal is a bet that long-term access to Venezuelan heavy crude can strengthen U.S. energy security and eventually ease costs for Americans. Whether it translates into relief at the pump will depend on how quickly Venezuela can turn its vast reserves into market-ready barrels.

articles.title: Ted Cruz defends Trump’s ‘accomplished’ Iran messaging, citing ‘multiple missions’
articles.summary: Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas) on Sunday said the U.S. is engaged in “multiple missions” in its conflict with Iran, defending the Trump administration’s efforts in the war that hit its six-month mark on Friday. NBC’s Kristen Welker on “Meet the Press” showed Cruz a graphic shared by President Trump on Truth Social stating, “Mission accomplished,”…
articles.body:
Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas) on Sunday said the U.S. is engaged in “multiple missions” in its conflict with Iran, defending the Trump administration’s efforts in the war that hit its six-month mark on Friday.

NBC’s Kristen Welker on “Meet the Press” showed Cruz a graphic shared by President Trump on Truth Social stating, “Mission accomplished,” alongside a smaller image of former President George W. Bush saying the same thing following the 2003 invasion of Iraq.

“Well, listen, I think there are multiple missions,” Cruz said in response. “If you look at the initial mission, which the Trump administration laid out, which is to degrade and eliminate Iran’s military capacity. Then, I think, the answer is unequivocally a yes on mission accomplished.”

Cruz added that the U.S. has “almost entirely destroyed” Iran’s drone and ballistic missile supply, that its “air force is in rubble on the runway, their navy is sunk at the bottom of the ocean, much of the senior leadership has been eliminated.”

“So in terms of military objectives, I think that is correct,” he continued. “Now, if you also look at the objective of imposing economic harm, right now, with the blockade that we are holding on Iran, Iran is facing $500 million a day of economic cost. That is enormous cost that is ratcheting up.”

Welker asked that if the mission has concluded, why hasn’t the president withdrawn U.S. service members. Cruz said that active combat military operations have “largely ceased” but that there “are occasional skirmishes.”

“The major operation now is the blockade. The blockade is imposing economic sanctions. And every day that pressure on the regime grows. I think economic sanctions are powerful.”

The U.S. has maintained a blockade on Iranian ports in the Strait of Hormuz in retaliation for Iran’s shutdown of the strait, cutting off roughly one-fifth of the world’s oil supply.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Monday shared few details about the Trump administration’s new economic warfare campaign, called “Operation Economic Outcast,” which followed Trump’s vow to hit Iran with an “Economic D-Day.”

Bessent urged other nations to cut off their financial ties to Iran or risk being cut out of the U.S. dollar system. Trump and State Department officials phoned their counterparts, calling on them to sever ties with the Iranian regime.

Iranian Economy Minister Ali Madanizadeh clapped back , warning that “the enemies should wait for an attack.”

articles.body:
Rep. Ro Khanna (D-Calif.) said Sunday that Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N.Y.) making a run for the presidency in two years wouldn’t affect his own potential choice to do so.

“If your fellow progressive Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez runs, will you still run?” CNN’s Dana Bash asked Khanna on “State of the Union.”

“It will have no bearing on my decision. Obviously, she’s extraordinary. But my vision is an economic vision. Look, Dana, one-third of the nation’s wealth is in my district, $20 trillion. We have five companies over a trillion dollars in my district. But where I grew up, in Bucks County, Pennsylvania, this economy of the future isn’t working for them,” Khanna replied.

“And I have a vision called economic patriotism, which calls for having the greatest economic mission in generations to build a future economy that’s going to be working for people I grew up with, deindustrialized communities, the Black South,” he added.

As this year’s midterms near, discussions around the next presidential election are heating up, with Ocasio-Cortez and Khanna among many Democrats being talked about as possible candidates for the 2028 race.

Both Ocasio-Cortez and Khanna making bids for the presidency in 2028 would follow a wave of progressive successes in this year’s primaries, from New York to Colorado. However, amid those wins, there has been pushback from more moderate figures in the party over issues like democratic socialist ideas and American support for Israel.

A few weeks ago, Sen. Jon Ossoff (D-Ga.), one of the other Democratic names floated as a 2028 presidential candidate, threw cold water on the idea .

“I have zero interest in running for president in 2028, and, frankly, zero interest in the 2028 fantasy football right now,” Ossoff told MS NOW’s Jen Psaki at the time.

articles.title: Massive AI boom puts one of America’s oldest manufacturers on path to double in size, CEO says
articles.summary: Corning is partnering with NVIDIA to build three optical-manufacturing facilities as AI data centers drive unprecedented demand for glass fiber.
articles.body: The race to build more data centers for artificial intelligence is driving demand for more than chips and electricity. It also requires vast networks of high-speed optical fiber to move data between servers, putting one of America’s oldest manufacturers at the center of the boom. Corning, the New York-based company best known to many Americans for its kitchenware and smartphone glass, is ramping up optical-fiber production as the data-center buildout accelerates. Nearly 175 years after its founding, the company is supplying a critical piece of the infrastructure behind the AI boom, the glass connections linking the servers inside the facilities powering it. ONE OF THE WORLD'S HOTTEST INDUSTRIES IS SPARKING A BLUE-COLLAR JOBS BOOM The company is partnering with NVIDIA to build three advanced optical-manufacturing facilities in North Carolina and Texas. The project is expected to create more than 3,000 jobs and expand Corning’s U.S. optical-manufacturing capacity tenfold. The investment offers a window into how the data-center boom is reaching well beyond the massive facilities themselves, creating demand for American factories and workers who make the equipment needed to keep them connected. CRACKDOWN ON CRITICAL TECH COULD OPEN AMERICANS TO A NEW NATIONAL SECURITY THREAT At a time when many Americans worry that artificial intelligence will replace human workers, Corning chairman, CEO and president Wendell Weeks said the opposite is happening inside one of the nation’s oldest manufacturers. "AI is a huge job creator, and it's a huge manufacturing job creator," Weeks told Fox News Digital. He said demand for Corning’s optical fiber is fueling the company’s fastest period of growth in nearly two centuries. "As a 175-year-old company, we're going through our fastest growth period," Weeks said. "We will probably double our size over the coming years and almost all of our new hires will be in advanced manufacturing, a significant part of them right here in America." That growth is already taking shape on Corning’s factory floors. "As the world develops and tells us what it needs, we're right there at the forefront," Emily Capek, planning supervisor at Corning’s Wilmington, North Carolina, facility, told Fox News Digital. She said employees are seeing firsthand how demand for AI platforms is driving demand for Corning’s products. FROM NETFLIX TO GPS: 10 WAYS THIS HIDDEN TECH INFRASTRUCTURE QUIETLY POWERS MODERN LIFE "Right now, the world needs our glass optical fiber to support the AI demand we're seeing," Capek said. "It's a great feeling on the factory floor." While much of the attention surrounding AI has focused on chipmakers and software developers, companies like Corning are supplying the glass technology that connects those systems and supports the industry’s rapid expansion. articles.title: Clyburn calls for expanding Supreme Court, says ’13 is a pretty good number’
articles.summary: Sen. James Clyburn (D-S.C.) on Sunday called for an expansion of the Supreme Court’s nine justices to 13, calling that increase a “pretty good number.” “Meet the Press” host Kristen Welker asked Clyburn if he agreed with former Vice President Kamala Harris’s request for court expansion in an interview. “Yes, I do,” the South Carolina…
articles.body:
Sen. James Clyburn (D-S.C.) on Sunday called for an expansion of the Supreme Court’s nine justices to 13, calling that increase a “pretty good number.”

“Meet the Press” host Kristen Welker asked Clyburn if he agreed with former Vice President Kamala Harris’s request for court expansion in an interview.

“Yes, I do,” the South Carolina Democrat said. “I think we are in a position now that calls for some significant actions taken by the Congress and we ought to expand, and 13 is a pretty good number. A baker’s dozen, it would be a good number to have on the court.”

Clyburn said the high court “has decided to reverse course and take this country back to those rulings of Justice Taney, that said, ‘No Black man has any right that white man must respect,'” referring to Supreme Court Justice Roger Taney, who wrote the majority opinion in the Dred Scott case in 1857.

“I had hoped that Clarence Thomas would follow the modern underpinnings of that Constitution of ours, but he has not done so,” Clyburn continued, referring to the justice nominated by former President George H. W. Bush. “In fact, he decided to go all the way from an angry leftist to a very angry rightist.”

Clyburn — who voted in favor of Thomas’s confirmation in 1991 and called him “my good friend” at the time while Clyburn served in the House — said he “absolutely” does not stand by the case he made for Thomas to be on the court.

“I had no idea that Clarence Thomas would rebel, the way he has, against his own background and experiences,” the senator said.

Other Democratic lawmakers have called for expanding the high court, including Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.). She wrote an op-ed for The Boston Globe in 2021 saying she did not “come to this conclusion lightly,” as she said she believed the “current court threatens the democratic foundations of our nation.”

Democratic lawmakers, including Sen. Ed Markey (D-Mass.), have attempted to expand the conservative-majority court through legislation without success.

After his failed reelection attempt in 2024, former President Biden called for term limits in addition to a binding code of ethics and a constitutional amendment to counteract the justices’ recent presidential immunity decision, after long resisting calls to change the court makeup.

Republicans have long opposed expanding the Supreme Court, accusing Democrats of attempting to “pack the court.”

articles.title: Trump indicates support for Christian-backed plan to help Canadian Jews escape antisemitism
articles.summary: Trump amplified a plan for expedited legal pathways for Jewish Canadians fleeing antisemitic persecution as Christian lawmakers press his administration.
articles.body: Jewish Canadians facing rising antisemitism might have President Donald Trump's support for an expedited legal pathway into the United States. Trump shared a report on the plan Sunday with his millions of followers on Truth Social, amplifying the appeal as Christian lawmakers and religious leaders press his administration to act because of a "disproportionate" amount of antisemitic incidents north of the U.S. border. The National Association of Christian Lawmakers (NACL) founder and President Jason Rapert told Fox News Digital from Israel on Sunday morning that he wants Trump to press Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney directly on the perceived "roadblocks" set up against the "quick recognition of the plight" of thousands of Jewish Canadians fearing for their safety. TORONTO POLICE INVESTIGATE GUNFIRE, VANDALISM TARGETING JEWISH-OWNED BAKERY CHAIN "We will find out" if Canada is getting in the way of the more than 2,000 Jewish Canadians who have expressed interest in relocating, Rapert said. "Trump should ask Carney right now," he added. "Canada should be embarrassed and ashamed of these perceived roadblocks. And we're trying to rally leaders to take a stand." The comments come after the NACL and its partners asked Trump to direct the State Department and Department of Homeland Security to create "lawful, secure, and appropriately expedited pathways" for Jewish Canadians and their immediate family members who face persecution or can credibly demonstrate fears for their safety because they are Jewish. TRUMP DOJ EXPANDS RELIGIOUS LIBERTY PROTECTIONS AFTER MAJOR SUPREME COURT RULINGS "For generations, America has served as a refuge for people fleeing religious persecution," the group wrote in a letter Thursday to Trump. "We urge you to ensure that, consistent with federal law and the security interests of the United States, that door remains open to our Jewish brothers and sisters in Canada who need it today." Rapert and former U.S. ambassador-at-large for International Religious Freedom Sam Brownback signed the letter along with more than 50 state legislators, religious leaders and other civic figures, sending it to Trump, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and congressional leaders. "Recent data demonstrate that Jewish Canadians are being targeted at a grossly disproportionate rate, while community-based reporting reflects thousands of antisemitic incidents across Canada," Rapert wrote. "These numbers represent more than statistics. They represent families who increasingly question whether they can safely send their children to Jewish schools, worship openly, display their faith publicly, or continue building their lives in communities where they no longer feel secure." ANTISEMITIC VIOLENCE ESCALATES AS DEADLY WEAPON ATTACKS SURGE IN 2025: REPORT Canada, which recently had a broadcaster reject the use of the word "terrorism" with regard to 9/11 coverage, has reported nearly 7,000 antisemitic incidents in a country of roughly 41 million people. By comparison, the U.S. has more than 342 million people and has reported fewer than 6,300, Rapert noted. "It's definitely a problem" by greater proportions in Canada, and "it's eerie to hear," he told Fox News Digital after a Sunday visit to the Ghetto Fighters' House Museum in northern Israel along with a delegation of U.S. lawmakers, where he spoke with a 91-year-old Holocaust survivor. CHRISTIAN LEADERS HOLD EMERGENCY SUMMIT IN JERUSALEM TO CONFRONT GLOBAL RISE IN ANTISEMITISM Rapert said the NACL was alerted of the concerns of the Jewish Canadians fearing their inability to emigrate to the U.S. from a piece in the National Post by Canadian/American Jewish community leader Michael Sachs, who is currently the Senior Director of the Jewish Federation of Tulsa, Okla. Jewish Canadians have expressed interest in relocating because of safety concerns, harassment, vandalism, intimidation, threats and violence against Jewish schools, synagogues, businesses, institutions and families following the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas terror attacks on Israel, according to Sachs. Now, amid Trump's frustration with Canada and Carney, Rapert sees the urgency for a proposal that would use existing refugee, humanitarian and visa authorities to help facilitate movement. ANTISEMITIC VIOLENCE REACHES DEADLIEST LEVEL SINCE 1994, NEW GLOBAL REPORT FINDS Carney has himself acknowledged a severe rise in antisemitism in Canada, saying his country has failed to adequately protect its Jewish community. "Canada’s civic compact is failing Jewish Canadians," Carney told an audience at Toronto’s Holy Blossom Temple in June, saying the country’s antisemitism crisis is "specific, severe and demands a targeted response." Carney said antisemitism in Canada had surged to levels not seen since the aftermath of World War II. More than two-thirds of religion-motivated hate crimes recorded in the previous year targeted Jewish Canadians, he said, despite Jews making up only about 1% of the country’s population. The prime minister pointed to bullets fired at Jewish schools, firebombings at synagogues, attacks on community centers and Jewish-owned businesses and the targeting of Jewish students on university campuses. MUSLIM BROTHERHOOD-LINKED NETWORKS EMBEDDED ACROSS CANADIAN INSTITUTIONS, NEW REPORT ALLEGES The NACL letter urged the administration to coordinate with state and local governments, Jewish organizations, churches, nonprofits and employers willing to help families establish new lives in the United States. "Antisemitism is a moral evil, and Christians must be willing to stand with our Jewish friends when they face hatred and persecution," Rapert said. "We are asking President Trump and his administration to consider what lawful steps America can take to help Jewish Canadian families who are genuinely concerned for their safety." Oklahoma has emerged as one potential destination. Jewish and Christian leaders in Tulsa have offered to help receive Canadian Jewish families, while Oklahoma Gov. Kevin Stitt has told Trump his state would welcome Jewish families who legally enter the United States, according to the letter. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "They bring talent, faith, family values, entrepreneurship, and a sincere desire to contribute to the Nation that offers them safety and religious liberty," the letter said. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: Clyburn says he backs El-Sayed: ‘All of us deserve second chances’
articles.summary: Sen. James Clyburn (D-S.C.) on Sunday said he supports Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed (D) after he apologized for comments he made following an attack on a Detroit-area synagogue earlier this year, with the South Carolina senator adding that “all of us deserve second chances.” El-Sayed told the Michigan Democratic Jewish Caucus at the state…
articles.body:
Sen. James Clyburn (D-S.C.) on Sunday said he supports Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed (D) after he apologized for comments he made following an attack on a Detroit-area synagogue earlier this year, with the South Carolina senator adding that “all of us deserve second chances.”

El-Sayed told the Michigan Democratic Jewish Caucus at the state party’s convention in Lansing on Saturday that he “made a mistake” after he said “violence is a cycle” and that “hurt people hurt people.”

“I have spoken with the good doctor. He’s our nominee. I support his election. I take him at his word. He has apologized. He says he will not campaign with Piker anymore. I’d say that it’s worth checking him at his word,” Clyburn told NBC News’s “Meet the Press” host Kristen Welker referring to left-wing Twitch streamer Hasan Piker.

“All of us deserve second chances,” Clyburn added.

El-Sayed made his remarks after the March attack on Temple Israel in West Bloomfield Township in Michigan, where authorities say a man intentionally drove a truck into the synagogue and injured a security guard to deliberately target Jewish people.

The man, identified by the Department of Homeland Security as Ayman Mohamad Ghazali , a naturalized U.S. citizen from Lebanon, lost family members in an Israeli attack in Lebanon earlier that month. Israel claimed that his brother was a Hezbollah commander .

El-Sayed said Saturday that he attempted to provide a broader context but acknowledged that doing so in the immediate aftermath of the attack was a mistake.

“If my statement caused pain, I’m sorry,” he said. “That was not what I intended.”

El-Sayed has also distanced himself from Piker , who threw his support behind the doctor on the campaign trail leading up to the Democratic primary. This outraged Democrats, citing the Twitch streamer’s past remarks saying that if American Jews promote the idea that they are “singularly invested in” Israel, then someone could one day “take action” against American Jews.

Piker has also said the political faction and militant group leading Gaza, Hamas, is a thousand times better than “the fascist settler colonial apartheid state” of Israel. He has argued that many of his controversial remarks are intentionally provocative and meant to challenge how people think.

El-Sayed recently told Semafor that Michigan voters are more focused on the cost of living and healthcare, calling the “effort to make this race about a streamer” living in Los Angeles “actually kind of laughable.”

The candidate, who narrowly defeated Rep. Haley Stevens (D-Mich.) in the primary, will face off against former Rep. Mike Rogers (R-Mich.) in November.

articles.title: Homan after Milo Yiannopoulos deportation: ‘Get them out quick’
articles.summary: White House border czar Tom Homan on Sunday said federal immigration enforcement authorities “get them out quick” after officials detained and swiftly deported far-right provocateur Milo Yiannopoulos last week. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) previously stated that Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detained the British national after he overstayed his visa. He was issued…
articles.body:
White House border czar Tom Homan on Sunday said federal immigration enforcement authorities “get them out quick” after officials detained and swiftly deported far-right provocateur Milo Yiannopoulos last week.

The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) previously stated that Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detained the British national after he overstayed his visa. He was issued a final order of removal by an immigration judge on July 22 after failing to appear at an immigration hearing.

“Once a judge orders them out, rather than being in detention, waiting for travel documents and flight arrangements, we –– ICE, along with the [Customs and Border Protection] and Department of Homeland Security, working really good on the efficiencies of the removal process,” Homan told CNN’s Dana Bash on “State of the Union” when asked if this process is standard.

“Get them out quick, open those beds up for more detainees to be held,” Homan added.

Homan said that because Yiannopoulos did not appear in immigration court, the judge ordered his deportation.

“So, once ICE gets an order of deportation from a federal judge, their job is to execute that order, and that’s what they did,” he said. “He had his due process, ordered removed by a federal judge, and ICE removed him. It’s that simple.”

Bash asked if right-wing influencer Laura Loomer tipped ICE off about Yiannopoulos’s status, to which Homan said “a lot of people tipped ICE off” and that Loomer “probably was.”

Bash then asked about DHS’s publicizing of Yiannopoulos’s arrest, release of a mugshot and saying in a statement that Yiannopoulos “chose to “overstay his welcome” and if this was all an attempt by the Trump administration to “make an example out of him to send a message?”

Homan reiterated “our goal” to “remove them as quick as possible, regardless of who they are,” and that the information released about the detaining was in response to “press inquiries.”

“We don’t deport people based on political affiliation,” Homan replied.

ICE apprehended Yiannopoulos Thursday night at the Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport in Kenner, La., ahead of a scheduled concert for Ye, the rapper formerly known as Kanye West, in New Orleans on Friday night, according to TMZ , which first reported his arrest.

Yiannopoulos previously worked on Ye’s 2024 presidential campaign and was an intern for former Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene (R-La.). The commentator was a vocal supporter of President Trump in 2016, praising his deportation agenda and immigration policies. He has also been criticized for past public remarks he has made about feminism and Islam.

He wrote for the conservative website Breitbart News before his resignation in 2017 after a video surfaced of him advocating for adult men and “younger boys” having sexual relationships. Yiannopoulos later apologized for the comments.

Yiannopoulos made several media appearances early in Trump’s first term, once appearing on “Real Time with Bill Maher” on HBO. The two appeared cordial, with Maher calling Yiannopoulos “a young, gay, alive Christopher Hitchens,” referring to the late Washington journalist and contrarian author.

articles.title: These are the most-searched slang words of 2026. How many do you know?
articles.summary: Unless you’re incredibly online – or incredibly in tune with Gen Z and Gen Alpha – it’s easy to fall behind on the latest slang.
articles.body:
(NEXSTAR) – Unless you’re incredibly online – or incredibly in tune with Gen Z and Gen Alpha – it’s easy to fall behind on the latest slang.

Describing yourself as “demure” or randomly interjecting with “skibidi” are so last year .

Word Unscrambler combed through Google search trends, analyzing which slang terms were looked up the most between January and August of 2026.

They found the top-searched word, which inspired more than 1.6 million queries, isn’t really a word at all. It’s actually a sequence of numbers.

OK, that one is pretty easy, but do you know the rest of the top 10?

The most searched slang words of 2026, according to World Scrambler, are:

6-7 : This one isn’t new to 2026, but it has had a long shelf life since kids started using it last year. 6-7, usually said with a hand gesture that imitates weighing two options (like the picture above), is a word that doesn’t really mean anything . These types of nonsense words are popular with Gen Alpha.

Chud : This is another one that isn’t new to the scene but is suddnely popular with Gen Alpha. It comes from the 1984 movie “C.H.U.D.,” which stands for cannibalistic humanoid underground dwellers, explains content creator Mr. Lindsay . Now, kids use it as another way to say “loser.”

Rizz : Short for “charisma,” having rizz means you’re charming, smooth, have good style or are otherwise attractive.

Gooning : The origins and some meanings of this one are X-rated, so use at your own risk, but its PG meaning is when someone gets lost or completely absorbed in an activity.

Cap, no cap : If something is “cap,” it’s a lie, or at least a big exaggeration. “No cap” means truthfully, honestly.

Mogging, mogged, mog, framemog, etc. : According to Merriam-Webster, to “mog” someone is outshine or outperform them. From that root slang word come the other variations, like “framemog” which means to make someone else look smaller by standing next to them with a larger, more muscular build.

Bop : Bet you thought you had this one, but double check yourself here. “Bop” used to be more commonly used to refer to a catchy song, but is now a “offensive, hurtful, and often misogynistic” piece of slang, according to Merriam-Webster , meaning a woman who has had many sexual partners.

Larping, larper : These terms derive from the acronym LARP, which is a live-action role-playing game. Larping can still mean you play one of those dress-up fantasy games, but it also can be used more broadly to describe pretending to be someone you’re not.

Aura, aura points, aura farming : Someone with aura is cool, stylish and has swagger. You earn “aura points” by more or less being cool. Aura farming is when you’re actively trying to look cool and earn those imaginary points.

Sigma : The 18th letter of the Greek alphabet, sigma in modern usage describes someone who is “coolly self-assured, independent, and driven,” according to Merriam-Webster. As opposed to an alpha male who has a pack, a sigma is more of a lone wolf.

articles.title: California bill recognizing 2 Islamic holidays nears Newsom’s desk
articles.summary: Gavin Newsom could soon decide whether California public schools and state workers get formal recognition of Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha holidays.
articles.body: California could soon formally recognize two of Islam’s most important holy days under legislation that would give state workers greater flexibility to take them off and allow public schools to close in observance of the holidays. The measure, which overwhelmingly passed the state Assembly and is awaiting Senate action, would recognize Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha in state law and could soon head to Democratic Gov. Gavin Newsom’s desk. Assembly Bill 2017, introduced by Democratic San Francisco Assemblymember Matt Haney, passed the Assembly 64-1 in late May. It must clear the Senate before the legislative session ends Monday to reach Newsom. TRUMP DOJ EXPANDS RELIGIOUS LIBERTY PROTECTIONS AFTER MAJOR SUPREME COURT RULINGS The bill would let state employees use existing paid holiday credits to take time off for Eid. Public schools and community colleges could also close for the holidays. "California is home to one of the largest and most vibrant Muslim communities in the country, and their traditions deserve recognition and respect," Haney said in a news release about the bill in March. "No student should have to choose between celebrating one of the holiest days of their faith and showing up to school, and no worker should feel they have to sacrifice their religious observance." Haney also said the bill is also about treating Muslim Californians equally. "AB 2017 is about making sure Muslim Californians are seen, valued, and treated with the same dignity as every other community in our state," he said. Eid al-Fitr, or the "Festival of Breaking the Fast," marks the end of Ramadan, the Islamic holy month when Muslims fast from dawn to sunset. Eid al-Adha, or the "Festival of Sacrifice," commemorates the willingness of the Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) to sacrifice his son in obedience to God. CALIFORNIA SCHOOL DISTRICT SUED OVER FIELD TRIP TO MOSQUE WHERE STUDENTS ALLEGEDLY DONNED MUSLIM GARB Supporters say the bill would make it easier for Muslim workers and students to take part in Eid prayers and spend the holidays with their families. "For decades, Muslim families across the state have had to navigate an unfair balancing act between their faith and their academic or professional obligations," Oussama Mokeddem, legislative and government affairs director for the Council on American-Islamic Relations’ (CAIR) California chapter, said in a statement in July. "AB 2017 is a meaningful step toward ensuring Muslim students can celebrate Eid with the same dignity, respect, and accommodation afforded to other faith communities." Hala Hijazi, founder of the Muslim Impact Council, recalled missing Eid with her family earlier in her career while working for the city of San Francisco. "It was really painful to not be with my family," Hijazi told the Sacramento Bee. She said her family would go to lunch after Eid al-Fitr services and give gifts to the children. The California Family Council, a conservative Christian advocacy group, opposes the bill’s school provisions, while saying it supports allowing students to take time off for religious holidays. FEDERAL COURT UPHOLDS TEXAS LAW REQUIRING TEN COMMANDMENTS IN PUBLIC CLASSROOMS The group objects to language allowing schools to hold exercises "acknowledging and celebrating the meaning and importance" of Eid. It also criticized a provision allowing the State Board of Education to develop a model curriculum guide for those exercises. "No California statute authorizes public schools to hold exercises celebrating the meaning of Christmas, Easter, or Good Friday," the group said in a May statement, arguing Christian and Jewish holidays have not received comparable treatment. "The asymmetry is written into the law." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP If signed into law, Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha would join other holidays California has recognized, including Lunar New Year and Diwali. California would not be the first state to recognize the Eid holidays. Washington was the first, according to the Sacramento Bee. Hijazi told the newspaper that California’s proposal would go further by allowing state workers to use paid holiday credits, while Washington allows unpaid time off.

articles.title: Merz: Germany coordinating Leipzig drone incident response with allies
articles.summary: Germany is coordinating its response to the drone incident at Leipzig Airport earlier this month with its European and NATO allies, Chancellor Friedrich Merz...
articles.body:
Germany is coordinating its response to the drone incident at Leipzig Airport earlier this month with its European and NATO allies, Chancellor Friedrich Merz said on Sunday.

The response from Berlin is "currently being finalized with the European Union and NATO partners," the chancellor told broadcaster ARD in his traditional summer interview.

Merz's government has yet to confirm who was responsible for the incident in Leipzig, amid widespread speculation that Russia could be behind it.

The chancellor refused to be drawn on the question, but said the investigation was nearing completion and that his government has agreed on how to respond.

A drone fitted with explosives and a detonation mechanism was discovered on the evening of August 4 in the security zone of Leipzig/Halle Airport, between Ukrainian cargo aircraft.

The Federal Public Prosecutor's Office has taken over the investigation, describing the incident as a "serious attack on transport and logistics infrastructure in Germany."

Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt later said Leipzig was "not an isolated case" but part of a broader pattern.

Security authorities have warned in recent years of "hybrid attacks" from Russia, with Germany and its NATO allies investing heavily to rearm to counter the threat from Moscow.

Merz was pressed in the interview on the spending spree on defence, with the budget for the German military, the Bundeswehr, set to leap from €82 billion ($95 billion) this year to €153 billion in 2028.

"We must rectify the shortcomings of the last 15 years," said Merz. "The Bundeswehr is not where it ought to be. We must be able to defend ourselves in Germany."

"What use is the best parental allowance to us if we lose our freedom and peace in Europe is jeopardized?" he questioned.

However, he also insisted that defence projects should become "much more cost-effective," announcing a fresh review of procurement procedures in coordination with Defence Minister Boris Pistorius.

The aim, Merz said, is a modern Bundeswehr.

"We do not want to fall back on old weapons systems," he explained. "We can see that technological development is advancing at a rapid pace, including in the defence industry."

New ideas are emerging at universities and research institutions, and defence start-ups are booming, the chancellor said.

"It doesn't have to be that expensive at all," he added, pointing to Ukraine's experience in developing low-cost defence projects such as drones in its war against Russia.

articles.title: Michigan GOP gubernatorial candidate says state’s elections are ‘ground zero for this republic’
articles.summary: Rep. John James (R-Mich.), who is running for governor in his state, on Sunday called upcoming Michigan elections “ground zero for this republic.” “We need to make sure that we stop socialism and that we save the state of Michigan, because if we don’t do it here, it’s going to go to the rest of…
articles.body:
Rep. John James (R-Mich.), who is running for governor in his state, on Sunday called upcoming Michigan elections “ground zero for this republic.”

“We need to make sure that we stop socialism and that we save the state of Michigan, because if we don’t do it here, it’s going to go to the rest of the country,” James told CBS News’s Margaret Brennan on “Face the Nation.”

“They’re campaigning with extremists who say that America deserved 9/11, and I think that coming up on the 25th anniversary of 9/11, these are statements that are way out of bounds and should definitely be clarified,” James said of some Michigan Democratic candidates, referring to 2019 comments from left-wing streamer Hasan Piker.

One of the candidates James was referencing, Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, has previously campaigned with Piker. However, El-Sayed recently said he had “no plans” to campaign with Piker, stepping in line with several Democratic lawmakers who have criticized the streamer over his remarks on American Jews backing Israel.

Piker has a history of controversial statements , including saying in 2019 that “America deserved 9/11,” which the streamer recently said he could have better phrased .

James’s comments come amid recent electoral success for democratic socialist and progressive insurgent candidates like El-Sayed in Democratic primaries, sparking some intraparty tension among Democrats over the future of their party.

El-Sayed himself has said he is not a socialist but has pushed for progressive policies like the abolition of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and Medicare for All.
